scenes.heading: Data Engineer vs Data Analyst
scenes.narration: Data engineers and data analysts work side by side, but they solve very different problems along the data journey.

scenes.heading: What each role owns
bullets: Engineers own pipelines, storage, and data reliability
Analysts own metrics, dashboards, and interpretation
Engineers write code and manage infrastructure
Analysts write queries and tell stories with data
scenes.narration: Engineers own the pipelines and storage because the business depends on data arriving reliably. Analysts own the metrics and dashboards because someone must translate data into decisions. Engineers lean on software and infrastructure skills, while analysts lean on querying and communication skills. Together they cover the full path from raw data to insight.

scenes.heading: Where they focus

left.label: Data Engineer
points: Ensures data is clean and available

scenes.narration: The engineer focuses upstream, making sure data is delivered clean, timely, and at scale. The analyst focuses downstream, using that prepared data to answer questions the business is asking. When the pipeline is solid, the analyst can trust every number they report.

scenes.heading: How they hand off
scenes.narration: The engineer builds a pipeline that lands clean data in the warehouse. The analyst then queries that data and shapes it into insight. That insight finally reaches decision-makers, closing the loop from raw source to business action.

scenes.text: Engineers make data trustworthy and available; analysts turn that data into decisions.
scenes.narration: The clearest way to remember the difference is that engineers build the road while analysts drive on it to reach a destination.
